title: Pub/Sub outbox publisher and shared GCP auth helper
story: As the platform team I want undelivered outbox rows published to Pub/Sub in (tenant_id, seq) order with orderingKey=tenant, idempotent on retry, so that the bus can leave the process.
valueDrivers: Event bus can scale beyond one process
requirements: ADR-001 zero dependencies; global fetch only
acceptance: src/core/gcp-auth.mjs exports createTokenProvider({fetch, env, now}) returning async getToken() using ADC via the metadata server (Cloud Run) with a documented GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN override for local use, caching until shortly before expiry; plus gcpFetch(tokenProvider, fetchImpl) helper adding Authorization. Uses only global fetch; no google libraries. Tested in gcp-auth.test.mjs with fake fetch (cache hit, expiry refresh, error path without leaking token in messages).

src/core/outbox-publisher.mjs exports createOutboxPublisher({port, readUndelivered, markPublished, now}) with a Publisher port {publish({topic, data, attributes, orderingKey})}; publishPending() orders rows by (tenant_id, seq), sets orderingKey=tenant_id, attributes include outboxId (the outbox row id) and tenant_id, marks rows published only after ack, stops a tenant at first failure to preserve order, and is safe to re-run (idempotent via outboxId attribute). Also exports createPubSubRestPublisher({tokenProvider, project, fetch}) building the Pub/Sub REST publish request (base64 data, orderingKey, attributes) tested against a fake fetch.

outbox-publisher.test.mjs passes: ordering across tenants and seq gaps, retry after failure publishes no duplicate outboxId for acked rows, per-tenant halt on failure while other tenants proceed, empty batch, request shape of the REST publisher.
bus.mjs and store.mjs untouched; in-process dispatch unchanged; rows are read through an injected function (shape documented from bus.outbox), not by editing core.

architecture/spikes/pubsub-outbox.md covers: ordering and orderingKey semantics, at-least-once with consumer dedupe via consumed_events, enable-message-ordering on topic, failure and resume-key behaviour, outbox retention, and a documented live-check command for the orchestrator (not under tests/). npm test never touches the network.
brief: Spike, small proof. First read src/core/bus.mjs and the outbox table (columns id, tenant_id, seq, type, payload, created_at, and any delivered marker; verify actual names, document them) but do NOT edit it; take rows via readUndelivered() injected function and markPublished(ids) so tests use plain arrays. gcp-auth.mjs is the ONE shared helper for real cloud calls: other spikes (S5-PLT-03) import createTokenProvider or accept a token-provider parameter, so keep its export names stable: createTokenProvider, gcpFetch. Metadata endpoint: http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token with header Metadata-Flavor: Google; response {access_token, expires_in}. Pub/Sub REST: POST https://pubsub.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/topics/{topic}:publish body {messages:[{data:base64, attributes:{...}, orderingKey}]}; response messageIds. Pub/Sub attribute values must be strings. Ordering pitfall: after a publish failure with an orderingKey, Pub/Sub requires resuming the key; document it and in the port expose optional resumePublish(orderingKey). Group per-tenant batches sequentially; do not parallelise within a tenant. Idempotency: attribute outboxId lets subscribers dedupe; publisher never relies on server dedupe. Synthetic project ids only (e.g. example-project). The live check is a documented command in the spike doc, not a script under tests/.

verdicts.reason: All criteria met; 10 ticket tests pass, bus/store untouched, e2e+security 0 fail matches baseline, doc complete, no token leaks
